Candidate design on identifiable viral coordinates

Source: R/model_eclipse.R
eclipse_design.Rd

Draws candidate trajectories on the coordinates the data determine – doubling time, peak capacity, clearance rate and inoculum – and derives the ODE rate constants from them. A box placed directly on \((\beta, \delta, p)\) forces \(\log_{10} K \ge 5.65\) for every candidate, so an established infection cannot peak low; the fitted population then acquires a spurious non-establishing family in its place.

Usage

eclipse_design(
  n,
  log10_K = c(3, 9.5),
  Td = c(0.3, 3),
  delta = c(0.05, 5),
  log10_V0 = c(0, 3),
  kappa = 4,
  c_clear = 10,
  T0 = 1e+07,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

n

Number of candidates.

log10_K

Range of the peak capacity \(K = p T_0 / c\), log10 scale.

Td

Range of the doubling time in days, sampled log-uniformly.

delta

Range of the infected-cell loss rate, per day.

log10_V0

Range of the inoculum, log10 scale.

kappa, c_clear, T0

Fixed constants, as in eclipse_trajectory().

seed

Optional seed, so a design can be reproduced exactly.

Value

A data frame of candidates with the identifiable coordinates and the derived beta and p.

Details

Because the doubling time is sampled positive, every candidate has \(r > 0\) and hence \(R_0 > 1\): the class-1 support consists of establishing kinetics by construction rather than by filtering fitted output. That is a property of the design, not a finding.

Examples

head(eclipse_design(5, seed = 1))
#>          Td            K     delta        V0         beta            p kappa
#> 1 2.3741652     53187.10 1.0695741  31.12417 2.826918e-05   0.05318710     4
#> 2 2.6411710    262304.26 0.9239559 142.18557 4.946214e-06   0.26230426     4
#> 3 1.3737859   5291110.87 3.4507631 945.62356 8.843079e-07   5.29111087     4
#> 4 1.2771306 800480275.42 1.9513134  13.80720 3.730490e-09 800.48027542     4
#> 5 0.3458657     20461.27 3.8607150 214.94912 5.164616e-04   0.02046127     4
#>   c_clear    T0
#> 1      10 1e+07
#> 2      10 1e+07
#> 3      10 1e+07
#> 4      10 1e+07
#> 5      10 1e+07
